name: afalg-then-splice
why: socket(AF_ALG) (a0=0x26, SOCK_SEQPACKET) followed by splice() in the same pid within 5s is the CopyFail syscall correlation
source: synthetic: shape of normalize() output for copyfail_behavioral.c (same-pid AF_ALG socket + splice(pipe->op_fd)); splice a1/a3 are the NULL off_in/off_out, exit is the decimal byte count

name: afalg-then-splice-window-edge
why: the same AF_ALG+splice pair 4s apart stays inside the 5s window; the correlation must still fire at the window edge
source: synthetic: a slower exploit, AF_ALG socket and splice 4s apart in one pid

name: cryptsetup-afalg-no-splice
why: cryptsetup opens an AF_ALG SOCK_SEQPACKET socket for LUKS keyslot decryption via the kernel crypto API and drives it with sendmsg/read, never splice; half the correlation, so the splice base must be required. (libkcapi's kcapi-hasher DOES splice for inputs >= 32 KiB and so fires: a real false positive, not a near-miss. The benign corpus does not model it yet; it is tracked in detections/RULE_DEFECTS.md, entry L8.)
source: recorded via source: cryptsetup lib/crypto_backend/crypto_cipher_kernel.c:62 socket(AF_ALG, SOCK_SEQPACKET, 0); no splice in the crypto backend

name: inet-socket-then-splice
why: an AF_INET (a0=2) socket plus splice() keeps both the socket() and splice() surface but is not the AF_ALG family; the a0=0x26 constraint inside the socket base must be load-bearing
source: synthetic: a proxy opening a TCP socket then splicing for zero-copy

name: afalg-and-splice-different-pid
why: the AF_ALG socket in one pid and splice() in another within 5s split the halves across processes; the pid group-by must enforce same-process
source: synthetic: AF_ALG socket in pid X, splice in unrelated pid Y

name: afalg-then-splice-too-late
why: the same pid opens an AF_ALG socket and splices 30s later, outside the 5s window; the timespan must bound the correlation
source: synthetic: a long-lived crypto daemon that splices unrelated data much later
